Use **`#7bacfc`** as the dark-mode primary. It's the closest color to `#3b82f6` that passes 4.5 as body text on `#1a1a2e`.

- **Contrast:** OKCA is 4.5 with `#7bacfc` as the foreground on `#1a1a2e`. That's the right direction for text on a dark surface. The check exited 0, so the color is in sRGB and the figure is a real measurement.
- **Brand `#3b82f6` fails as it stands:** it scores only 1.9 on `#1a1a2e`.

**Changing lightness alone can't fix it.** `#3b82f6` is a very saturated blue, and at that saturation sRGB has no shade lighter than about L 0.648. The best lightness-only result is `#438aff`, which scores 2.2 and still fails. To reach 4.5 the color has to give up some saturation as well as get lighter.

| | `#3b82f6` | `#7bacfc` |
|---|---|---|
| Lightness (OKLCH) | 0.623 | 0.743 |
| Chroma | 0.188 | 0.128 |
| Hue | 259.8° | 259.8° |

The hue is unchanged, so it's still recognisably the brand blue. The shift from the brand color is a deltaE of 13, which counts as "clearly different" on the perceptual scale, not a subtle nudge. It's a lighter, softer blue. This is a brand call, so please have the art director sign off on it.

I didn't check this against any other dark surfaces you may have.

I built the 4×3 grid myself because `klar variants --light-steps 4 --chroma-steps 3` fails here: 9 of its 12 cells fall outside sRGB. Blue at full chroma (0.188) only exists between L 0.466 and L 0.648, so I chose the lightness steps to sit inside that band.

All 12 cells are in gamut and keep the hue of #3b82f6 (259.8°). Each ratio is OKCA with the shade as text on `#ffffff`, measured with `klar contrast <shade> "#ffffff"`. Body text needs 4.5 or more.

| OKLCH L | Low chroma (C 0.008) | Mid chroma (C 0.058) | Full chroma (C 0.188) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.64 | `#898c91` 2.7 ✗ | `#788db0` 2.7 ✗ | `#4087fc` 2.7 ✗ |
| 0.58 | `#777a7f` 3.5 ✗ | `#667b9d` 3.5 ✗ | `#2d74e7` 3.5 ✗ |
| 0.52 | `#66696e` 4.6 ✓ | `#556a8b` 4.6 ✓ | `#1961d2` 4.6 ✓ |
| 0.47 | `#585b5f` 5.8 ✓ | `#485b7c` 5.8 ✓ | `#0251c1` 5.8 ✓ |

- **What passes:** the bottom two rows (6 of 12) pass body text on white. The top two rows fail.
- **Large text:** the L 0.58 row (3.5) clears the large-text and UI threshold of 3.0. The L 0.64 row (2.7) fails that too.
- **Chroma doesn't affect the score:** the ratio is the same across a row, so lightness alone decides pass or fail. Chroma only changes how saturated the shade looks.
- **Brand blue:** #3b82f6 itself (L 0.62, C 0.188) is between the top two rows and fails on white. The nearest full-chroma shade that passes is `#1961d2`.
- **Gamut limit:** the grid is lightness-limited by the full-chroma column, so there are no very light or very dark rows. For wider lightness range, the adaptive `klar variants` grid is not a uniform 4×3, and its cells aren't laid out as a grid of equal lightness steps.

Five accents that all pass 4.5 for body text on `#ffffff`. I measured each with OKCA as foreground on background.

| Accent | Hex | OKCA on white |
|---|---|---|
| Red | `#c20329` | 4.7 |
| Orange | `#a84c03` | 4.5 |
| Green | `#017835` | 5.0 |
| Blue | `#2052dc` | 5.0 |
| Purple | `#7f24d0` | 5.0 |

- **Distinctness:** I checked all 10 pairs with deltaE. The closest are red/orange and blue/purple at 18 and 19, and the rest are 39 or higher. Anything above 11 reads as clearly different.
- **Orange:** `#a84c03` sits right at the 4.5 threshold. It only got there by trading a little saturation, and it is deltaE 3 from a truer orange (`#b45309`), which is barely noticeable. If you'd rather not have it sitting on the line, a slightly darker orange gives some margin.
- **Amber and yellow:** none pass as text on white. `#a16207` topped out at 4.1, so a yellow-ish accent would have to be a brown or be used only for large text or non-text elements. That's why the fifth hue is orange rather than amber.
- **Extra option:** teal `#0f766e` (4.8) also passes, but it's only deltaE 18 from the green, so I left it out to keep the set clearly different.

Getting hex values for the three fixes that need a chroma change.

Seven of the 12 real foreground/background pairs fail AA body text (4.5) in `tokens-system.json`. I measured OKCA as foreground on background with klar. Every proposed fix re-measures at 4.5 or above, and none is applied to the file yet.

## Results

| Background | Foreground | OKCA | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#ffffff` | text `#1a1a2e` | 15.8 | pass |
| `#ffffff` | muted `#666666` | 4.8 | pass |
| `#ffffff` | primary `#3b82f6` | 2.9 | **fail** |
| `#ffffff` | accent `#e94560` | 2.8 | **fail** |
| `#ffffff` | success `#22c55e` | 1.9 | **fail** |
| `#1a1a2e` | inverse `#ffffff` | 16.5 | pass |
| `#1a1a2e` | primary `#3b82f6` | 1.9 | **fail** |
| `#1a1a2e` | accent `#e94560` | 2.0 | **fail** |
| `#1a1a2e` | success `#22c55e` | 3.4 | **fail** |
| `#1a1a2e` | muted `#666666` | 2.4 | **fail** |

Two pairs are skipped because the foreground is the same color as the background: `text` on `surface-dark` and `inverse` on `surface`. Those are the wrong pairings for those tokens, not failures.

## Proposed fixes

I measured how much each color changes with deltaE. Under 3 is imperceptible, 5–10 is noticeable, 11–20 is clearly different, and over 20 is very different.

**Lightness alone is enough (hue and chroma are kept):**

| Pair | Fix | New OKCA | deltaE |
|---|---|---|---|
| primary on white | `#3b82f6` → `#115bcc` | 5.0 | 15 |
| accent on white | `#e94560` → `#bf103f` | 4.7 | 13 |
| success on dark | `#22c55e` → `#41d870` | 4.8 | 5 |
| muted on dark | `#666666` → `#919191` | 4.7 | 17 |

**Lightness alone can't reach 4.5, so the color has to lose saturation:**

| Pair | Fix | New OKCA | deltaE |
|---|---|---|---|
| success on white | `#22c55e` → `#047f38` | 4.6 | **22** |
| primary on dark | `#3b82f6` → `#7bacfc` | 4.5 | 13 |
| accent on dark | `#e94560` → `#fe8a93` | 4.6 | 14 |

The success green on white moves 22 deltaE, which is a visibly different green. That needs a design decision.

## Things to know

- **Each color needs a light and a dark value.** The fixes for one background make the color worse on the other. The darkened primary `#115bcc` would fail on the dark surface, and the lightened `#7bacfc` would fail on white. In practice that means separate light-mode and dark-mode tokens for `primary`, `accent`, `success` and `muted`.
- **Muted is the odd one out.** `#666666` passes on white at 4.8, so only its dark-mode variant needs fixing.
- **The README names a different file as the source of truth.** It says `tokens.json` is the source of truth, and that file has different colors, in OKLCH. I audited `tokens-system.json` as you asked and did not check `tokens.json`. Its `success` token, `oklch(0.7 0.3 150)`, is outside sRGB, so any figure for it would describe a mapped color rather than the token as authored.

I can write the fixes into the token file as `-on-light` and `-on-dark` variants, or audit `tokens.json` next, if you want either.
